title: Usage Fingerprint Joiner for Subsecond Billing Attribution
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Problem: As we expand streaming and multi-model routing, downstream billing consumers are seeing inconsistent attributions (duplicate token counts, split attributions between fallbacks, and missing tokens from early stream chunks). Existing batch reconciliations lag and create noisy invoices and manual adjustments. This ticket adds a small, low-latency 'usage fingerprint joiner' service in Console backend that generates canonical, deduplicated, and attributable usage records in subsecond time, suitable for immediate chargeback and real-time dashboards.
proposed_solution: Introduce a stateful joiner service that consumes enriched event fragments from the serving runtime (stream-chunk events, finalization events, route-change events) and emits canonical usage records to the billing topic. Key ideas: (1) compute a deterministic fingerprint for each logical request (request_id + route + model_variant + start_offset) and merge fragments using sequence numbers; (2) keep a short-lived windowed state (Redis with TTL or RocksDB local store) to handle reorders and late fragments (default 30s); (3) idempotent upserts into the billing Kafka topic using dedupe keys and monotonic sequence; (4) augment records with routing provenance (primary/fallback, cache_hit, quantization_profile) so downstream pricing rules can apply; (5) provide a verification tunnel that mirrors outputs to an internal validation topic for offline reconciliation to catch regressions.
acceptance_criteria: P95 join latency < 50ms under baseline traffic (10k req/s)
Deduplication reduces duplicate token attributions to < 0.1% compared to raw events
Attribution correctness: parity >= 99.9% vs existing batch-reconciler over 24h test window
No increase in end-to-end request tail latency for API customer requests (measured at edge) > 1ms
Feature-gated rollout with canary and automatic revert on error rates > 1%
rollout_plan: 1) Feature-flagged roll out to internal traffic only with validation mirrors. 2) Canary to 5% tenant traffic in a single region for 48 hours. 3) Compare mirrored outputs to batch-reconciler; require acceptance criteria. 4) Gradually ramp 5%->25%->100% with health gates and automated rollback on mismatches. 5) After 7 days of stable operation, flip billing consumers to use canonical topic and deprecate the older stream-with-duplicates path.
tasks: Schema: add fingerprint_key, seq_num, partial_flag, provenance fields to protobuf (billing.proto)
Runtime: change serving runtime to emit fragment metadata (next ticket will be created) and wire to event topic
Joiner Service: implement windowed state, merge logic, and Kafka producer with idempotent keys
Storage: evaluate Redis vs RocksDB for hot-window; prototype both and measure p99 memory/latency
Integration tests: synthetic stream with reordering and duplicates and end-to-end validation harness
Dashboard: create telemetry - join_latency, duplicates_detected, reorders_handled, mirror_mismatch_rate
Documentation: developer guide for billing consumers & runbook for rollbacks
progress_notes: 2026-02-12: Spike completed comparing Redis vs RocksDB; Redis faster for <50ms window but memory pressure grows with tenant fanout. Decided to prototype hybrid: local RocksDB + Redis as optional hot-shard cache.
2026-02-20: Protobuf schema draft uploaded: link in links. Initial review by @morgan and @jamal; asked to add provenance fields for fallback_reason.
2026-02-28: Prototype joiner can process 5k req/s on a developer box with p95=28ms (no compression). Memory profile acceptable for 30s TTL at 10k req/s per instance with local RocksDB.
2026-03-05: Security reviewed the design; flagged requirement to redact PII from mirrored validation topic. Added transformation step before mirror publish.

2026-03-10: First canary deployed to internal tenants under feature flag. Mirrored outputs generated; initial mirror_mismatch_rate=0.07% vs batch-reconciler. Investigating edge-case with partial streaming close to TTL boundary.
